PoseToki · Drawing guide

Three-minute seated poses: contact and overlap

A seated figure is not simply a standing figure folded at the waist. Find where weight meets the seat, where the thighs leave the pelvis, and which leg passes in front. Pose PT049 gives you a clear contact point to start from.

Updated October 2, 2026

Three points to find before drawing

  1. The torso's orientation differs from the head's gaze. A turned neck does not mean the entire rib cage turns by the same amount.
  2. Find where the pelvis rests on the stool seat. If that contact drifts, even accurately drawn legs will not feel seated.
  3. Compare the overlapping knees and the shoe on the floor. Resolve the nearer leg's visible edge first; leave hidden parts undrawn.

These reference photos were generated for PoseToki with AI. Use them to practice observation, not as anatomical ground truth.

Draw the same pose at three speeds

  1. 30 seconds

    Place the stool seat as a short horizontal line and a simple pelvic mass on top. Mark only head and foot positions before stopping.

  2. 1 minute

    Connect rib cage, pelvis, and both knees. Draw the nearer leg's outline first and only the visible portions of the rear leg.

  3. 3 minutes

    Check torso rotation, foot-to-floor contact, and stool-leg direction. Add fingers and clothing folds only after the structure reads clearly.

A common mistake—and a correction

Drawing both overlapping legs as complete shapes can make the thighs seem to pass through one another. Establish one front contour, then break the rear line wherever it is hidden. Record the boundaries visible in the photo instead of inventing every concealed edge.

Transfer the idea to another pose

Start pose PT052 with the stool seat and pelvis, exactly as you did for pose PT049. Only then add the long reaching arm and torso tilt. Beginning at the fingertips makes it easy to lose the body's seated stability. In a comic panel, mark the weight-bearing surface before removing the chair from your sketch.

Questions for your review

  • Does the pelvis visibly meet the seat?
  • Does the front-to-back order of the legs match the photo?
  • Can you read the seated direction without arm and face details?

Try it in the studio

Set the studio to 3 minutes and 5 poses. Whenever a seated pose appears, spend the first 30 seconds only on seat and pelvis. On other poses, ask the same question: where does this body touch or lean on something?
